pictures.scene: Sorolla, Fisherman Carrying a Net — a barefoot fisherman in a yellow headcloth and a dark jacket hung with cork floats strides up the stony shore with a long brown net looped over his shoulder and trailing away behind him across the grass, the white huts and bare masts of the fishing village standing along the skyline under a tall bank of cloud, on one occasion, while jesus was standing by the lake of gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on him to hear the word of god, he saw two boats at the edge of the lake, the fishermen had left them and were washing their nets
pictures.name: pd_sorolla_netten

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ in the Storm on the Lake of Galilee — a small fishing boat pitches bow-up onto a breaking wave with its sail torn loose and its prow buried in white spray, some of the men hauling on the ropes and clinging to the mast overhead while the rest crouch low in the stern around Christ, who sits quietly among them in the dark under the flying clouds, jesus got into the boat belonging to simon and asked him to put out a little from shore, and sitting down, he taught the people from the boat, when jesus had finished speaking, he said to simon, put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_christ_in_the_storm_on_the_lake_of_galilee

pictures.scene: Homer, The Herring Net — a fisherman in dark oilskins and a round hat leans far out over the side of his dory hauling a loaded net up out of the green swell, the mesh hanging heavy with silver herring that spill over the gunwale in front of him, his mate half hidden behind the net at the stern and a red buoy riding the water below, master, simon replied, we have worked hard all night without catching anything, but because you say so, i will let down the nets, when they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear
pictures.name: pd_homer_the_herring_net

pictures.scene: King David Kneeling Before an Altar — a crowned king in steel armour under a stiff gold embroidered cope kneels on the bare floor with one hand laid flat on his breast and his bearded face lifted, his harp propped against his knee and an open book held out to him from the right, a white-robed angel sweeping down out of the cloud at the upper left, so they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink, when simon peter saw this, he fell at jesus' knees, go away from me, lord, he said, for i am a sinful man
pictures.name: pd_king_david_kneeling_before_an_altar

pictures.scene: Israels, Children of the Sea — three fisherman's children wade barefoot through the thin water running up the flat sand, the eldest carrying the smallest on his back while the little girl in a white cap holds on to his arm and drags a stick behind her, their toy boat with its small sail riding the shallows at the left, for he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken, and so were his partners james and john, the sons of zebedee, do not be afraid, jesus said to simon, from now on you will catch men
pictures.name: pd_israels_kinderen_der_zee

pictures.scene: Burnand, The Disciples Peter and John Running to the Tomb — two men lean into a run side by side against the yellow light of the early morning, the younger ahead in a white robe with his hands clasped at his chest and his hair blown straight back, the grey-bearded older man beside him in red and dark blue with his hand pressed over his heart, both of them staring hard ahead, and when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed him, while jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy, when he saw jesus, he fell facedown and begged him, lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean
pictures.name: pd_burnand_disciples_running_colour

pictures.scene: Victors, Hannah Praying in the Temple — an old woman in a wide pleated red hat and a heavy fur-trimmed robe stands in the shadow of the temple with her worn hands folded tightly together and her eyes raised, a starched white collar at her throat and a gold clasp holding her mantle shut, the stone piers and the dark grille of the sanctuary standing behind her, jesus reached out his hand and touched the man, i am willing, he said, be clean, and immediately the leprosy left him, do not tell anyone, jesus instructed him, but go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them
pictures.name: pd_victors_hanna_biddend_in_de_tempel

pictures.scene: Church, Twilight in the Wilderness — long banks of burning red cloud stream the whole way across the sky above an empty range of wooded hills, the last clear yellow light lying flat along the horizon behind them, a still dark lake holding one small wooded island below, with pines and broken rock closing in the near shore, but the news about jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear him and to be healed of their sicknesses, yet he frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray
pictures.name: pd_church_twilight_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Liebermann, The Twelve-Year-Old Jesus in the Temple — a boy in a plain pale robe and sandals stands on the stone floor of the temple inside a ring of seated teachers in their prayer shawls, one old man leaning forward over his knees to listen and another bent close with a hand raised to his mouth, more men crowding along the rail and the stair in the brown shadow behind, one day jesus was teaching, and the pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, people had come from jerusalem and from every village of galilee and judea, and the power of the lord was present for him to heal the sick
pictures.name: pd_liebermann_jesus_im_tempel

pictures.scene: Bogdanov Belsky, At the School Doors — a boy in a patched coat and bound bast shoes leans against the open doorpost of a village schoolroom with his stick in his hand and his bundle still on his shoulder, looking in at the class of children bent over their desks under the hanging lamp, the blackboard and the wall map just inside and the scrubbed plank floor running away in front of him, just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat, they tried to bring him inside to set him before jesus, but they could not find a way through the crowd, so they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of jesus
pictures.name: pd_bogdanov_belsky_at_school_doors

pictures.scene: Guercino, Christ Questioned by the Elders — Christ in a red tunic and a deep blue mantle stands with His hand lifted and one finger pointing across His chest, looking steadily past the white-bearded old man in heavy gold who leans in close at His shoulder, a man in a dark hat pressed up against the left edge and other hands gripping each other below, when jesus saw their faith, he said, friend, your sins are forgiven, but the scribes and pharisees began thinking to themselves, who is this man who speaks blasphemy, who can forgive sins but god alone
pictures.name: pd_guercino_aanklagen

pictures.scene: Koninck, An Old Scholar at His Desk — an old man in a wound cloth cap and a heavy fur-lined gown sits bent close over the table trimming his quill with a small knife, a large book lying open in front of him under the one fall of light, loose papers and an inkstand on the cloth at his elbow and the cold dark room standing empty behind him, knowing what they were thinking, jesus replied, why are you thinking these things in your hearts, which is easier, to say, your sins are forgiven, or to say, get up and walk
pictures.name: pd_koninck_old_philosopher

pictures.scene: Ostade, The Cottage Dooryard — a farmhand in a broad black hat stands in the open doorway of the thatched cottage pulling his coat straight as he steps out into the yard, an old woman in a white cap sitting on a low stool beside him shelling beans into her lap over a red dish of them on the ground, a boy in a hat playing with a black and white dog at the paling fence on the right and a hen scratching the swept earth in front, but so that you may know that the son of man has authority on the earth to forgive sins, he said to the paralytic, i tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home, and immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying god
pictures.name: pd_ostade_dooryard

pictures.scene: Reymerswaele, The Tax Collectors — a tax officer in a huge red fur hat and a blue gown leans low over his open ledger with spectacles slipping down his nose, writing an entry with a long quill and a heavy ring on his finger, a second man in a green cap crowding in over his shoulder with his face screwed up to point down at the page, counting coins out on the table with his other hand under the shelf of rolled papers and the candlestick behind, everyone was taken with amazement and glorified god, they were filled with awe and said, we have seen remarkable things today, after this, jesus went out and saw a tax collector named levi sitting at the tax booth, follow me, he told him
pictures.name: pd_reymerswaele_the_tax_collectors

pictures.scene: Lievens, The Feast of Esther — a young queen in a pearl crown and a long gold veil sits at the banquet table in a blue and white gown stiff with gold embroidery and heavy chains, turning to speak with her hand raised open at her breast, a dark-bearded man in a plumed hat listening close at the left with his hand lifted, a broad gold pie and a torn loaf of bread set out on the white cloth in front of them against the pale drawn curtain behind, and levi got up, left everything, and followed him, then levi hosted a great banquet for jesus at his house, a large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them
pictures.name: pd_lievens_het_feestmaal_van_esther

pictures.scene: The Doctor at the Child's Bedside — a grey-bearded doctor in a black coat sits forward on a low chair with his chin resting on his hand, watching a sick red-haired child who lies asleep on a pillow across two chairs under a striped yellow blanket, the father standing silent in the shadow at the back of the dark cottage room with a small framed picture and an empty ladderback chair between them, but the pharisees and their scribes complained to jesus' disciples, why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners, jesus answered, it is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick
pictures.name: pd_tomanek_the_doctor

pictures.scene: Perov, The Monastery Refectory — a rich lady in a wide lilac silk gown and a pale shawl sweeps through the vaulted hall on the arm of a decorated old gentleman, two black-robed monks bowing and gesturing her forward while a third lies stretched flat on the stone floor in front of her, a barefoot beggar woman on the right lifting both hands from the ground with her children huddled against her, the painted arches and the leaded window standing over the whole crowd, i have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance, then they said to him, john's disciples and those of the pharisees frequently fast and pray, but yours keep on eating and drinking
pictures.name: pd_perov_kloostermaaltijd

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Peasant Wedding — the bride sits quiet with her hands folded and her eyes lowered under a paper crown hung on the green cloth behind her, the long table in front of her crowded with guests eating and drinking from wooden bowls and earthenware jugs, two servers carrying a door laid with bowls of porridge across the barn floor while a man in a red cap reaches to lift them off, the straw of the stacked harvest filling the wall above, jesus replied, can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while he is with them, but the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them, then they will fast
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_peasant_wedding

pictures.scene: Israels, The Little Seamstress — a young girl in a pink lace cap and a blue bodice sits sideways on a rush-seated chair with a great fall of white linen heaped across her lap and running down to the floor, both hands holding the cloth up close to take her stitch, her head bent over the work in the quiet light of the bare cottage wall and the scrubbed red tiles under her feet, he also told them a parable, no one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one, if he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old, and no one pours new wine into old wineskins, if he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined
pictures.name: pd_israels_het_naaistertje

pictures.scene: Lhermitte, The Grape Harvest — a young vintager in a dark bodice and a blue apron stands at the end of the row with one hand on her hip, holding out a heavy wicker basket piled with black grapes, a picker bent low over the vines beside her and another woman in a white headcloth working in the shade of the chestnut tree, a fair-haired child sitting on the ground at her feet eating a grape and looking up at her, the autumn slopes running away behind, instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins, and no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, the old is better
pictures.name: pd_lhermitte_wijn

lines.text: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,
He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.
When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.
Master, Simon replied, we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.
When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus' knees. Go away from me, Lord, he said, for I am a sinful man.
For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,
and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. Do not be afraid, Jesus said to Simon. From now on you will catch men.
And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.
Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. I am willing, He said. Be clean! And immediately the leprosy left him.
Do not tell anyone, Jesus instructed him. But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.
But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.
One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there.
People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.
Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,
but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith, He said, Friend, your sins are forgiven.
But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?
Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, Your sins are forgiven, or to say, Get up and walk?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins... He said to the paralytic, I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.
And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, We have seen remarkable things today.
After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. Follow Me, He told him,
and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.
But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus' disciples, Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?
Jesus answered, It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.
Then they said to Him, John's disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.
Jesus replied, Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?
But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.

He also told them a parable: No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.
Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.
And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, The old is better.
